test_policy.notes: USF requires official results for at least one of the SAT, ACT or CLT from freshman applicants (including international applicants). Minimum subsection scores: SAT 490 EBRW and 480 Math; ACT 19 Reading, 17 English and 19 Math; CLT 38 Verbal Reasoning + Grammar/Writing and 16 Quantitative Reasoning. USF superscores across test dates and does not consider the optional essay section. Scores must come directly from the testing agency (not the Common App, a counselor or a screenshot); for Summer/Fall admission they must be taken before December. USF's CDS (C8A) also lists SAT or ACT as required.

requirements.supplemental_essays: None. The four application steps are the application, the $30 fee or a waiver, STARS (or official transcripts) and SAT/ACT/CLT scores.
requirements.notes: Apply with USF's own online application or the Common App (no preference). Pay the nonrefundable $30 fee or submit an ACT, CLT, SAT or Common App fee-waiver request (reviewed case by case). Submit STARS (Self-Reported Transcript and Academic Record System) after applying; students with high school coursework outside the U.S. may not need STARS but must submit official transcripts and exam results (secondary education of 12-13 years with a diploma or certificate). USF recalculates the GPA from core academic courses, adding quality points (AP, IB, AICE and dual enrollment +1.0, honors +0.5, C or better). Recommendations, essay and interview are not requested; the CDS (C7) marks them, and every non-academic factor, 'Not Considered'. Final transcripts are required after admission. Applications are evaluated for all three terms (Fall, Summer, Spring) and fall is the most competitive.

deadlines.label: Early Action (non-binding) application deadline, Fall/Summer 2027
deadlines.notes: Same deadlines for international applicants living outside the U.S. Decision types: admit, deny or defer. Early Action gives the best chance at the preferred campus and term and automatic consideration for merit scholarships.

deadlines.label: Early Action materials deadline (application fee or waiver, test scores, STARS)
deadlines.notes: Materials are due after the application deadline.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision application deadline, Fall/Summer 2027
deadlines.notes: Materials deadline January 15, 2027. Decision types: admit, waitlist or deny. Same dates on the international page.

deadlines.label: Scholarship consideration deadline (application, test scores, transcripts and fee all complete)
deadlines.notes: Automatic consideration for merit scholarships (including the out-of-state / Green and Gold waivers for international students); no separate scholarship application. Also the Regular Decision materials deadline.

deadlines.label: Rolling application deadline, Fall/Summer 2027
deadlines.notes: Materials deadline March 15, 2027; decisions rolling from early March (admit or deny). Admission becomes more competitive as the deadlines pass.

english_policy.waiver_notes: International students from non-English-speaking countries must show English proficiency through minimum SAT, ACT or CLT section scores: SAT Reading and Writing 490 or higher; ACT English 17 and Reading 19 or higher; CLT Verbal Reasoning and Writing 38 or higher. USF states it does not accept English proficiency tests such as TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo as substitutes for these minimums.

english.notes: 'We do not accept English proficiency tests such as TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or others as substitutes for these minimum test score requirements.'

aid.notes: Merit awards only for international freshmen: all admitted students are automatically considered if the application is complete by January 15, 2027 (no separate application; funding is limited; notified by postal mail). Out-of-state merit tuition waivers for non-Florida residents: Green and Gold Presidential Waiver about $44,000 (up to $11,000 per year), Directors about $36,000 (up to $9,000 per year), Scholars about $20,000 (up to $5,000 per year); they apply only to out-of-state tuition. CDS H6: institutional non-need-based aid is available to nonresidents (1,187 recipients, average $10,001). USF says most international students do not qualify for FAFSA; the USF Foundation offers privately funded scholarships with a separate application.
